Working notes:

- Routing depends on request type, size, and region; no reliable general mapping can be inferred yet.
- Option C (regional office) was accepted for:
  - Small shipment, north region (REQ-2408)
  - Large shipment, north region (REQ-2409)
- Option C was rejected for:
  - Large claim, north
  - Small invoices from east, north, and south
  - Small claim from south
  - Small refund from south
- Other tested outcomes were all rejected:
  - A for small claim, south
  - B for large claim, north
  - D for large shipment, south
- Do not assume urgency, requester department, or note wording determines the correct option; the available examples do not establish this.
- For future tickets, distinguish shipment vs. claim/invoice/refund and region before choosing. C currently has evidence only for north-region shipments, not as a universal choice.

Working notes:

- Routing cannot yet be mapped reliably from request type, size, region, requester, urgency, or note wording alone. Identical/similar requests have produced different outcomes.
- Accepted:
  - C (regional office): small shipment, north (REQ-2408); large shipment, north (REQ-2409); small shipment, south (REQ-2414)
  - D (external partner): small claim, east (REQ-2416)
- Important contradiction: C was rejected for another small shipment from north (REQ-2412), so even a previously successful type/region/size combination is not determinative.
- Rejected examples include:
  - A: small claim south; small shipment south; small refund east; small invoice east
  - B: large claim north; large refund east; small claim south
  - C: large claim north; small invoices east/north/south; small claim south; small refund south; small shipment north
  - D: large shipment south; small refund south; small refund north
- Previously recorded rejections remain valid: C for small claim south, small refund south, and invoices across east/north/south; A for small claim south; B for large claim north; D for large shipment south.
- Do not treat urgency, repetition, requester department, wording, or stated origin (“through regional office”) as a reliable routing rule.
- For future tickets, record all attributes and outcomes, but avoid generalizing from isolated successes. No option is currently safe to choose universally; C has successes for some shipments, and D has one success for a small east claim.

Working notes:

- Routing remains non-deterministic from request type, size, region, requester, urgency, wording, repetition, or stated origin alone. Similar/identical requests can yield different outcomes.
- New accepted outcomes:
  - A: large refund, south (REQ-2422)
  - C: large shipment, south (REQ-2423, REQ-2427); small shipment, north (REQ-2424)
  - D: large claim, east (REQ-2428)
- New rejected outcomes:
  - B: small invoice, north (REQ-2420)
  - A: small invoice, south (REQ-2421); large refund, south (REQ-2426)
  - C: large invoice, north (REQ-2425)
  - D: large claim, south (REQ-2429)
- Contradictions reinforce that combinations are not determinative:
  - Large refund south was accepted by A and rejected by A on another ticket.
  - Large shipment south was accepted by C despite an earlier D rejection.
  - Small shipment north has both C success and C rejection.
- Consolidated known successes:
  - C: small/large shipment north; small shipment south; large shipment south.
  - D: small claim east; large claim east.
  - A: large refund south.
- Known rejections include:
  - A: small claim south; small shipment south; small refund east; small invoice east/south.
  - B: large claim north; large refund east; small claim south; small invoice north.
  - C: large claim north; large invoice north; small invoices east/north/south; small claim south; small refund south; small shipment north (one ticket).
  - D: large shipment south (one ticket); small refunds south/north; large claim south.
- Do not infer rules from urgency, repetition, department, wording, or “through regional office.”
- Record every attribute and result. No option is universally safe; avoid overgeneralizing isolated successes.

- Routing is non-deterministic. Request type, size, region, requester, urgency, wording, repetition, stated origin, department, or “through regional office” do not determine the correct option. Similar or identical requests can produce different outcomes.
- Record every attribute and result; do not generalize from isolated successes. No option is universally safe.

Known successes:
- C: small/large shipment north; small shipment south; large shipment south; large shipment east; large refund east.
- D: small claim east; large claim east.

Recent rejections:
- A: large claim north; large claim south; small refund south.
- B: large claim south.
- D: large invoice north.

Important contradictions:
- Large refund south was accepted by A and rejected by A on different tickets.
- Large shipment south was repeatedly accepted by C, despite an earlier D rejection.
- Small shipment north has both C success and C rejection.
- Large claim south was rejected by B and A on separate tickets.
- Repeated requests and urgency do not reliably change routing: “second attempt,” client follow-ups, and end-of-day requests produced mixed results.

- A: small claim south; small shipment south; small refund east; small invoice east/south.
- B: large claim north; large refund east; small claim south; small invoice north.
- C: large claim north; large invoice north; small invoices east/north/south; small claim south; small refund south; small shipment north (one ticket).
- D: large shipment south (one ticket); small refunds south/north; large claim south; large invoice north.

- Recent evidence further confirms contextual notes are unreliable: “same as last month,” regional-office origin, second attempt, client follow-ups, and end-of-day urgency all produced mixed outcomes.

Known successes:

- B: small refund south.
- C: small shipment north; large shipment east; large shipment south.
- D: small claim south; large claim east.
- Prior successes remain: C small/large shipment north; small shipment south; large shipment south; large shipment east; large refund east. D small/large claim east.

Recent rejections:
- B: small shipment south.
- C: small refund east; large claim south.
- Prior rejections remain: A large claim north/south, small refund south; B large claim south; D large invoice north.

Important contradictions:
- Small shipment north: C accepted and rejected on different tickets.
- Large shipment south: C repeatedly accepted, despite an earlier D rejection.
- Large refund south: A both accepted and rejected.
- Small claim south: D now accepted, despite earlier A/B/C rejections.
- Small refund south: B now accepted, despite earlier A/C/D rejections.
- Large claim south: A, B, and C have all rejected it on separate tickets.
- Large invoice north: A accepted, while B/C/D previously rejected it.
- Repetition, urgency, client follow-ups, and regional-office wording do not reliably change routing.

Working notes:

- Routing remains non-deterministic. Request type, size, region, requester/department, urgency, wording, repetition, stated origin, and follow-ups do not reliably determine the option. Identical or similar requests can produce different outcomes; no option is universally safe.
- Record every ticket’s full attributes, chosen option, and result. Treat prior successes only as weak evidence, not rules. Contextual cues such as “same as last month,” regional-office origin, second attempt, client follow-ups, scanned paperwork, and urgency have shown no dependable effect.

Recent successes:
- A: small invoice south (REQ-2450, REQ-2455).
- B: small refund south (REQ-2454).
- C: large shipment east (REQ-2456); small invoice south (REQ-2458); small invoice east (REQ-2459).
- D: small claim south (REQ-2457).

Recent rejections:
- A: large refund north (REQ-2451); large invoice north (REQ-2452); large refund east (REQ-2453).
- Existing rejections include B small shipment south and large claim south; C small refund east and large claim south; D large invoice north.

Important contradictions:
- Small invoice south: A and C both accepted.
- Small invoice east: C accepted.
- Small shipment north: C accepted and rejected on different tickets.
- Large shipment south: C repeatedly accepted despite an earlier D rejection.
- Large refund south: A both accepted and rejected.
- Small claim south: D accepted despite earlier A/B/C rejections.
- Small refund south: B accepted despite earlier A/C/D rejections.
- Large claim south: A, B, and C rejected it separately.
- Large invoice north: A previously accepted but now rejected; B/C/D also rejected it.
- Large refund east: A now rejected despite a prior success for that request category/option.
